deep.reconstruction:
Context: This is a fragment of an axiomatic, neutral (pre-parallel-postulate) build-up of elementary geometry, numbered Lehrsätze 2-6. The previous page (Lehrsatz 6) proves the exterior-angle inequality from the equality version proved here. The next page carries Gauss's 1813 remark that the theory of parallels is the 'partie honteuse' of mathematics. The setting is three-dimensional: spheres (Kugelfläche) here and a cone on the previous page replace the circles of plane geometry. From the red-pencil notes and the uses in the proofs, the cited theorems are: Satz 2 = Euclid I.5 (in a triangle, equal sides give equal opposite angles); Satz 3 = its converse, Euclid I.6 (equal angles give equal opposite sides); Satz 4 = a triangle cannot have two right angles.

Lehrsatz 5. In a triangle ABC, no angle equals the exterior (supplementary) angle at another vertex. Let D lie on line CB beyond B. Claim: angle ACB ≠ angle ABD.

Proof by contradiction. Assume angle ACB = angle ABD (H). Three cases.

Case I (AB = AC, Fig. 1).
- By Satz 2, angle ABC = angle ACB.
- With H, angle ABC = angle ABD.
- But angle ABC + angle ABD = 2R, two right angles (adjacent supplementary angles; this step is implicit).
- So angle ABC = R and angle ACB = R: two right angles in one triangle, contradicting Satz 4.

Case II (AB < AC, Fig. 2).
- B lies inside the sphere S with centre A and radius AC; C lies on S.
- The line CB, extended beyond B, must meet S again at a point E on the far side of B. So E lies on ray BD, with B between C and E.
- AE = AC, so by Satz 2 in triangle AEC: angle AEC = angle ACE, i.e. angle AEB = angle ACB.
- By H, angle AEB = angle ABD.
- Since E lies on ray BD, angle ABD = angle ABE.
- So angle AEB = angle ABE in triangle ABE. By Satz 3, AB = AE = AC, contradicting AB < AC.

Case III (AB > AC, Fig. 3).
- C lies inside the sphere S' with centre A and radius AB.
- The line BC, extended beyond C, meets S' at E, with C between B and E.
- AE = AB, so by Satz 2 in triangle ABE: angle ABE = angle AEB.
- From H, taking supplements (my explicit step: equal angles have equal supplements): angle ACE = 2R − angle ACB = 2R − angle ABD = angle ABC.
- Since E lies on ray BC, angle ABC = angle ABE, which equals angle AEB = angle AEC.
- So in triangle ACE, angle ACE = angle AEC. By Satz 3, AC = AE = AB, contradicting AB > AC.

Hence angle ACB ≠ angle ABD. QED.

The red-pencil notes at the bottom map the numbering ('Satz 2 = Eucl. Satz 5') and appear to state Satz 4, 'in einem Δ können nicht zwei [rechte Winkel sein]'. Their remaining fragments ('Grundlinie ... ∞') look like further lemma statements and are not recoverable.

The point of the method: Euclid's own proof of I.16 needs a midpoint and doubling construction. Here the only existence ingredient is that a line through an interior point of a sphere meets the sphere on both sides of that point. This is an ordering and infinitude-of-lines assumption; the result fails in elliptic geometry, where exactly this assumption fails.
errors: No mathematical error found; all three cases are valid.
Implicit steps (not errors): (a) in Case I, angle ABC + angle ABD = two right angles; (b) in Case III, equal angles have equal supplements, so H gives angle ACE = angle ABC.

Implicit geometric assumption: a line through an interior point of a sphere meets the sphere in a second point lying on the other side of that point. This is the neutral-geometry content that excludes elliptic geometry; it is used without proof (presumably from earlier definitions).

Wording slip in Case III: the original line 'da man aus der Voraussetzung ... folgt' was overwritten to 'folglich ... zugleich (Satz 2)', leaving slightly ungrammatical but clear logic. The final '= AEB' wraps to the next line.

results.what: No interior angle of a triangle equals the exterior angle at another vertex, proved by case analysis on AB vs AC using an auxiliary sphere and the isosceles theorem and its converse (no parallel postulate)
results.modern_name: Equality case of the Exterior Angle Theorem (Euclid I.16) in neutral/absolute geometry
results.usually_credited_to: Euclid (Elements I.16); neutral-geometry status emphasised by Saccheri, Legendre, Bolyai, Lobachevsky

results.what: Method: proving the exterior-angle theorem in space, via spheres (here) and cones (Lehrsatz 6) instead of Euclid's midpoint construction, as part of an axiomatic foundations-of-geometry sequence
results.modern_name: Alternative proof of Euclid I.16 in absolute geometry, in a spatial/metric (sphere-based) foundation
results.usually_credited_to: Not standardly attributed; sphere-based foundations of geometry are associated with Gauss's own notes on defining the plane, and later Bolyai and Lobachevsky

results.what: Citations: Satz 2 = Euclid I.5 (isosceles base angles), Satz 3 = Euclid I.6 (converse), Satz 4 = no triangle has two right angles
results.modern_name: Pons asinorum and converse; corollary of absolute geometry

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss's work on the foundations of geometry and parallels is well documented (Werke VIII), and the result is Euclid I.16. The only mildly notable feature is the spatial, sphere/cone-based proof inside a systematic neutral-geometry sequence, consistent with Gauss's known interest in foundations around 1813.
